data.body:
FIXES bug B38f7effd99 (R-scalability finding 2). Extend load_scope so a CLI command shares one State for its whole run; a write verb re-reads only the tail. Rule r-single-load. SIZE S, RISK low. FALSIFIER/REGRESSION TEST: a test counting fold calls shows more than 1 per read verb (fails against the unfixed code). Divides the 2 to 5 times multiplier. CONFORMANCE (r-upgrade-safe, r-replay-compat, r-derive-dont-store, r-derived-cache-bounded, r-bounded-everything, r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-unavailable-not-pass, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scale-answers, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-scalability): the event log is never rewritten or truncated; every cache is derived, local and rebuildable; old logs replay identically; a new knob defaults to the old behaviour; an upgrade note ships with the change; a measurement that could not run is unavailable; a fix carries a regression test that fails against the unfixed code.

ACCEPTANCE ADDED (assessment 2026-11-13): the real defect is read_all, not fold: fold is already called once per verb, but read_all is called next 2, show 2, status 3, doctor 15 times. The test pins those counts to 1 per read verb through the counters of PF-verb-read-counters, and also covers the re-read inside limit_for (see PF-plan-memo-per-load). Priority is already 10 (higher than P1 = 80); no change.

NOTE 2026-10-18 (RH-contradictions-2026-10-18, contradiction #34): Re-cited governing decisions: D-compat-r2, D-unify-r2 and D-enum-fallback in place of the superseded D-compat, D-unify and D-enum-fallback-strict. Same meaning.

ORIGINAL TEXT (before RH-contradictions-2026-10-18):
WHAT: `ddflow --version`, `--help` and every hook subcommand currently import the whole CLI: cpu 0.53 s for `import ddflow.surfaces.cli` (-X importtime: ddflow.api 0.56 of 0.62 s total, ddflow.api.knowledge 0.18, ddflow.api.ci 0.18, ddflow.config 0.07, jinja2 0.04, services.export 0.06, upgrade_apply 0.07) against 0.04 s for bare Python, measured under load (about half idle). Make command dispatch lazy: the registry maps a command name to a module path and imports that module only when invoked (argparse parser construction from declared data stays cheap, or the parser for one command is built on demand); keep jinja2/tomlkit lazy until first use; hooks import only infra.log, the redactor and the session service. WHY: R-perf-profile-2026-10-11; it is the floor of every agent action that runs a ddflow process (SessionStart, UserPromptSubmit, git hooks, every CLI call). D-compat: no behaviour change; the existing hoisting work (R9ce3581787: 36 deferred imports hoisted) pushed the other way - cycles stay broken through the registry, not function-local imports, and the earlier tests that forbid function-local imports must keep passing. INTERFACE TO REUSE: surfaces/registry.py and declared/ tables, the single parser source of CLI+MCP parity (mcp.py must still list all 112 tools from the same table). TESTS: failing-first import-budget test: `python -X importtime -c 'import ddflow.surfaces.cli'` imports no module under ddflow.api/ddflow.services except those the command needs (assert by module set, not by milliseconds, so it is load-proof) plus a measured-budget check through B-perf-bench; full CLI/MCP parity and help-text goldens unchanged. SIZE: medium (~300 lines, touches hot files: expect to wait for B-hot-files). ACCEPTANCE: `ddflow --version` cpu under 4x bare Python startup on the same machine; before/after table in a research record; no golden changed.

Test-suite duration extension 2026-10-12 (R-test-duration-2026-10-12): the suite spawns the CLI through 4,635 run_cli call sites in 378 test files (a real python -m ddflow each, 0.615 s for --version measured), 245 cpu-minutes in all; on the 4-vCPU CI runner that is the 78-minute run. Lowering the cold start is worth a measurable share of suite time: add the suite's cpu-minutes (fix-test-duration-profile report) to this task's before/after table. Removing the calls is fix-test-duration-cut; the two stack.

OPERATOR 2026-10-17 (D-unify-deps-r2): lazy loading is the method of the whole performance phase: besides import time, the goal is the smallest memory footprint and fastest startup; coordinate with B-perf-memory-footprint and B-perf-lazy-deps (dependencies imported at the point of use, including the new required PyYAML).

Related: PS-lazy-embed (bug B4c7b7e8d5b, 8.2 s CPU on --version). MERGE PROPOSAL (note only, operator decides): AU-startup, B-perf-lazy-cli and EX-startup-budget overlap on import time and could be one task.

ASSESSMENT 2026-11-13: ddflow --version still costs 1.1 s and imports 912 modules; every test process spawn pays it (4,635 spawns x 1.1 s). Pin: use the len(sys.modules) budget of PF-verb-read-counters as this task's regression pin. LAY-services-acyclic is only a soft relation, not a need. Priority is already 19 (higher than P1 = 80); no change.

R-scalability L. doctor takes about 870 s; py-spy shows 76 percent in verified_level -> harness.verify -> find_all, which rescans 1264 transcripts (1.3 GB) and a Kilo SQLite table once per consumed ask (228 asks). Index transcripts once per doctor run; memoise by (ask, file, mtime, size). Complements FOC-doctor-slow and UX-doctor-budget (quick mode and budget): not a duplicate, this removes the rescan. SIZE S-M, RISK low. FALSIFIER: doctor over 60 s idle on the big log, or its output differs. CONFORMANCE (r-upgrade-safe, r-replay-compat, r-derive-dont-store, r-derived-cache-bounded, r-bounded-everything, r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-unavailable-not-pass, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scale-answers, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-scalability): the event log is never rewritten or truncated; every cache is derived, local and rebuildable; old logs replay identically; a new knob defaults to the old behaviour; an upgrade note ships with the change; a measurement that could not run is unavailable; a fix carries a regression test that fails against the unfixed code.

ASSESSMENT 2026-11-13 (architecture report, doctor profile 273 s): scope is the transcript rescan (67.7 s in approvals/harness.find_all, 41 s of it docindex.read_only_rows). Doctor costs not yet in any task, to cover here or in UX-doctor-budget: brief.brief inside doctor 61.9 s; surfaces/mcp/_instructions fill 34.7 s; approvals/overrides.rows 54.4 s; 15 read_all calls (see PS-single-load). FOC-doctor-slow is done although doctor still takes 94-108 s; its falsifier was 14 minutes.

R-scalability: decide_then_append re-runs the read and fold inside the global append lock whenever the mark moved (inferred from code and 8 s board lock waits, not measured). Use the checkpoint so the locked section is a mark compare plus a tail. Measure lock hold first. SIZE M, RISK medium. FALSIFIER: append-lock hold p95 over 100 ms with 20 writers. CONFORMANCE (r-upgrade-safe, r-replay-compat, r-derive-dont-store, r-derived-cache-bounded, r-bounded-everything, r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-unavailable-not-pass, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scale-answers, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-scalability): the event log is never rewritten or truncated; every cache is derived, local and rebuildable; old logs replay identically; a new knob defaults to the old behaviour; an upgrade note ships with the change; a measurement that could not run is unavailable; a fix carries a regression test that fails against the unfixed code.

ASSESSMENT 2026-11-13: related to TX-fold-in-lock-ratchet, which ratchets and converts the sites that read or fold inside log.transaction() (29 sites per the architecture report); do the conversion there, this task makes the locked section a mark compare plus a tail once the checkpoint exists. It stays behind PS-state-checkpoint.

Rule r-perf-budget. BUDGET, p95 at 1M events on an idle machine (today at 132k): --version 0.3 s wall (1.0 s wall, 8.2 s CPU); hooks 0.3 s p50; show/list/gate status/next 2 s (6 to 18 s); status and brief 3 s (22 and 40 s); board 3 s and output-capped (9 to 18 s); recall/search 2 s (15.5 s); write verbs claim/heartbeat/complete 2 s with append-lock hold under 100 ms; merge 5 s (git-bound); doctor quick 10 s, --full 5 min time-bounded (about 870 s); rebuild index 5 min, verify 10 min, replay 10 min (linear is acceptable); RSS of read verbs 500 MB (580 to 700 MB); derived data on disk at most 3 times the log size (about 5.2 GB). The existing D-perf-index 2 s budgets for status/next/brief are breached by 5 to 20 times. RATCHET: (1) fixture from PS-bench-fixture; (2) HARD-GATED deterministic counters: folds per command, events parsed, git subprocesses, bytes read, modules imported, events appended by read verbs (must be 0), append-lock hold; (3) timing is user CPU normalised by a calibration loop, min of 3 runs, plus or minus 25 percent band; wall time is informational only; (4) slope test at N and 4N, ratio under 2 for O(item) verbs; (5) shrink-only baseline tests/perf/baseline.json refreshed by pins regenerate, budgets as [perf] knobs; (6) CI: 100k tier in the unit gate (under 60 s), 1M tier as a nightly cadence job; ENFORCEMENT starts as warn for 2 weeks, then block (r-safe-by-default). Builds on B-perf-bench, FOC-log-ceiling, PM-budgets; not a duplicate. SIZE M, RISK low. FALSIFIER: a seeded 2x slowdown or an extra fold passes the gate. CONFORMANCE (r-upgrade-safe, r-replay-compat, r-derive-dont-store, r-derived-cache-bounded, r-bounded-everything, r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-unavailable-not-pass, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scale-answers, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-scalability): the event log is never rewritten or truncated; every cache is derived, local and rebuildable; old logs replay identically; a new knob defaults to the old behaviour; an upgrade note ships with the change; a measurement that could not run is unavailable; a fix carries a regression test that fails against the unfixed code.

ASSESSMENT 2026-11-13: part (2), the hard-gated deterministic counters, does not need the fixture (counts are independent of log size) and is delivered now by PF-verb-read-counters on a small fixture. This task keeps the wall and CPU budgets, slope test and tiers, which stay behind PS-bench-fixture.

R-scalability H. Parse is 1.8 s of 2.8 s cold (13.7 us per event). Keep raw JSON until a handler needs data, and use orjson when installed (2 to 4 times is a published figure, not measured here). Output byte-identical; no new hard dependency (r-no-eager-heavy-import). SIZE S-M, RISK low. FALSIFIER: cold parse not 1.5 times faster, or any output differs. CONFORMANCE (r-upgrade-safe, r-replay-compat, r-derive-dont-store, r-derived-cache-bounded, r-bounded-everything, r-everything-configurable, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-unavailable-not-pass, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scale-answers, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-scalability): the event log is never rewritten or truncated; every cache is derived, local and rebuildable; old logs replay identically; a new knob defaults to the old behaviour; an upgrade note ships with the change; a measurement that could not run is unavailable; a fix carries a regression test that fails against the unfixed code.

RE-BASELINE 2026-11-13 (architecture report): the cold read is now 4.07 s, of which json.loads is only 1.85 s; the rest is object construction and merge. Measure the FALSIFIER (cold parse 1.5 times faster) against this 4.07 s read, not the earlier 1.8 s of 2.8 s.

Assessment 2026-11-13 (architecture report, item 13).

data.body:
A harness that runs a scripted ddflow session as a subprocess and SIGKILLs it at a named step (after claim, mid-gate, between git merge and worktree.merged, after worktree.merged before complete, mid event write), then runs a fresh 'agent' (resume + brief) and asserts: no event lost or glued, the item continues from its last good state, no duplicate merge, no double-counted review round, and the final log replays to the same state. Part of P-test-robustness; an invariant ratchet so a new multi-step action must register its crash points.

ASSESSMENT 2026-11-13: related to FI-writer-kill-soak (24 writer processes, random SIGKILL at the log layer, bounded lock hold); the log-layer kill points belong there, this task covers the claim, gate, merge and complete steps; share the kill-point registry rather than building two.

ddflow --version takes 1.1 s because 829 ddflow modules import first; ddflow.api costs 866 ms of 907 ms; every hook call pays it. Lazy per-verb imports, a fast path for --version and hook calls, and an import-time budget ratchet. ALSO COVERS the UX proposal UX-lazy-imports (next on a small project under 300 ms). Do the UX-latency-profile table first if it exists. SIZE M, RISK medium. FALSIFIER: --version over 0.4 s (target 0.3 s). CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-everything-managed, r-reuse-core, r-adapters, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, r-unavailable-not-pass, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-audit-code): the fix lands with a regression test that fails against the unfixed code; ratchets are shrink-only baselines; a check that could not run is unavailable.

MERGE PROPOSAL (note only): overlaps B-perf-lazy-cli and EX-startup-budget; see PS-lazy-embed.

ASSESSMENT 2026-11-13 (workflow report): the pre_tool hook costs 1.09 s per Bash call, 0.86 s of it imports; this task is the fix and the -X importtime numbers in that report are its baseline. Priority raised from 100 to 19 (the value of its overlap sibling B-perf-lazy-cli; lower runs sooner) so it is not stuck behind the cap-held items; a named claim also bypasses the cap. The merge of the three overlapping startup proposals (B-perf-lazy-cli, EX-startup-budget, this one) is left to the operator.

What cannot be seen today: a refused claim and why (lock waits) is not an event; time waiting for the operator (approvals, questions) is not measured; tool-call and idle time per lane live only in the transcripts (P-agent-memory capture); review and gate cost is spread over events. Add the few missing events (claim.refused with the blocking item and glob, ask.waited when the ask engine exists) with upcasters, and derived views for per-item state durations, queue wait, rework (reopen, gate re-run, review rounds), lane starvation. ddflow observe signals lists every signal, its source and its freshness; an unreadable signal is UNAVAILABLE, never zero. Reuses B-gap-metrics for the replay.

RELATED 2026-11-02: PM-cycle-split reports stages that need claim-refusal and human-wait events as not measured until this lands; PM-store holds the series.

NARROWED 2026-11-13 (workflow report): human-wait time is no longer in scope. The premise that ddflow records no event for time spent waiting on a person is stale: WF-sli-approval-flow derives approval wait, unspent approvals and merged-open age from the existing ask and merge events (no new events, so no ask.waited). This task keeps claim refusals (claim.refused with the blocking item and glob), per-state durations, queue wait, rework, lane starvation, and gate and review cost.
data.title: Close the telemetry gaps: claim refusals, per-state durations, rework, gate and review cost as events or derived views, with a list of signals and their freshness

CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-tell-dont-discover, r-no-shell, r-safe-by-default, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-audit-ux): every new limit, budget or default is a knob with a check; refusals name the next call in CLI and MCP form; nothing new is CLI-only unless person-only; new enforcement ships warn or off; docs change with the code.

RESCOPED 2026-11-13 (docs-ux report): ddflow emits no colour today (the only escape in ddflow/ is the clear-screen in the lanes watch view; none in views), so the NO_COLOR falsifier passes already and honouring it is a no-op. What remains is a small pin test so colour cannot be added later without the switch, plus accepting --no-color as a no-op. The 80-column readability part moved to UX-term-width.
data.title: Pin that ddflow emits no colour escapes (NO_COLOR, non-TTY, --no-color accepted); width at 80 columns is UX-term-width

data.body:
R-maintainable-code, size S, wave 0. ACCEPT: a fixture doc with a missing path, a dead relative link and a nonexistent command example fails the check with line numbers; on ddflow the 16 stale ARCHITECTURE.md paths are reported. FALSIFIER (must fail on unfixed code): docs check extracts surfaces but does not resolve paths.

LAYOUT CAUTION 2026-11-13 (docs-ux report, verified): ddflow/services/docscheck.py already exists as a module, and the globs above create the package ddflow/services/docscheck/. A package and a module of the same name collide (the package wins on import and hides the module). Before claiming, decide the layout: either a sibling module such as ddflow/services/docscheck_paths.py, or convert docscheck.py into the package with the old module's names re-exported; then fix the globs.

Decision D-scope-focus-2026-11 (4). ddflow start detects (no .ddflow, empty repo versus history) and runs the right stage of init, adopt or onboard; init and adopt print start as the next step; adopt --agents defaults to the agents it detects and asks when none are found (replaces UX-adopt-detect). Offers the light pipeline profile from UX-light-profile when it exists. SIZE S-M, RISK low. FALSIFIER: one command on a fresh repo reaches doctor healthy; a Claude-only repo gets Claude files only. CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-tell-dont-discover, r-no-shell, r-safe-by-default, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-audit-ux): every new limit, budget or default is a knob with a check; refusals name the next call in CLI and MCP form; nothing new is CLI-only unless person-only; new enforcement ships warn or off; docs change with the code.

ACCEPTANCE ADDED 2026-11-13 (docs-ux report, both gaps verified today): (1) a CLI ddflow setup command as the alias of the MCP ddflow_setup, for mode parity (r-mode-parity): today ddflow setup answers 'not a command'; (2) a description for ddflow init --help, which prints only the bare usage line. Also confirmed: adopt --agents defaults to all 27 agents rather than the detected ones.

R-maintainable-code, size M, wave 0. Tools from the stack table (vulture, knip, cargo udeps, deadcode); read-only per r-review-proposes; missing tool is unavailable (r-unavailable-not-pass). ACCEPT: a fixture with an unused function yields a proposal via the stack tool; a missing tool yields unavailable; the pass edits nothing. FALSIFIER (must fail on unfixed code): the ddflow AST ratchet sees only module-level Python functions, so a JS fixture reports nothing.

SCOPE ADDED 2026-11-13 (docs-ux report): include a knob-reader check against the config register: eta.coverage_bar and pins.mergiraf_keep_pct showed no readers in the assessment. This is unverified for dynamic access (getattr, string-built keys), so the finding is a proposal that names the access pattern it could not see, never a deletion.

ddflow --help is a flat 80-name list printed twice. Group into Plan, Work, Review, Learn, Operate, Admin; default view shows the 12 common verbs; --all shows everything. SIZE S, RISK low. FALSIFIER: claim and gate are in the default view; a new-user test finds them without the README. Reuse COMP-tree. CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-tell-dont-discover, r-no-shell, r-safe-by-default, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-audit-ux): every new limit, budget or default is a knob with a check; refusals name the next call in CLI and MCP form; nothing new is CLI-only unless person-only; new enforcement ships warn or off; docs change with the code.

WORDING FIX ADDED 2026-11-13 (docs-ux report, verified): the top-level help blurb for export says 'list, print, enable, disable, --diff ...' but ddflow export list is an error (unknown document kind 'list'); a bare ddflow export is what lists. Correct that line while regrouping the help.

PROPOSED DEFAULT, awaiting operator confirmation: the README is 470 KB (about 117000 tokens). Split it by Diataxis into a short README (under 300 lines) plus tutorial, how-to, reference and explanation pages, as ONE single-owner task with the README FROZEN for other agents while it runs (other tasks must wait or edit the new pages afterwards). The generated reference stays generated. SIZE L, RISK medium (large diff, link rot). FALSIFIER: README under 300 lines, doc links check passes, first run found in under 30 s. Reuse docs check. CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-tell-dont-discover, r-no-shell, r-safe-by-default, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-audit-ux): every new limit, budget or default is a knob with a check; refusals name the next call in CLI and MCP form; nothing new is CLI-only unless person-only; new enforcement ships warn or off; docs change with the code.



STATE 2026-11-13 (queue fix-up): phase P-readme is done and the README is now 114111 B / 1648 lines (was 470 KB); the under-300-lines falsifier is still unmet, so this task stays open, narrowed to what P-readme did not do. Operator to confirm or close.

NOTE 2026-11-13 (docs-ux report): docs/guide/adoption.md lines 5-27 still lead with the uvx ddflow-mcp config although the README says ddflow-mcp is not on PyPI yet (line 9 carries a caveat, but the uvx block comes first); lead with the git install there while the split runs, and fold the fix into this task or UX-audience-guides.
